Leticia Gutierrez

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 9, Harris County, Texas · Open seat

Environmental justice advocate; government relations and community outreach director

Leticia Gutierrez is a Democrat from east Houston and an environmental justice advocate who has worked in government relations and community outreach. This is her first run for public office. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for the redrawn Texas 9th Congressional District with 53.6% of the vote, and she faces Republican Alex Mealer in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Gutierrez stands

Immigration
Supports what she calls a "more humane immigration policy": a secure border paired with a pathway to citizenship for immigrants who entered illegally but have lived in the U.S. for a long time.
Health care
Lists health care access among her main campaign priorities.
Cost of living
Makes everyday affordability for families a central part of her platform.
Infrastructure and storms
Calls for infrastructure that holds up better after storms.
Government spending and corporate subsidies
Says the government has been giving subsidies to large corporations while working families pay the bill.
Environment
Pushes for cleaner air and water in east Harris County and for economic development that protects longtime residents near industry. She says this work began when her son developed asthma.

Background

  • Democratic nominee, U.S. House Texas District 9 (2026); won March 3, 2026 primary with 53.6%
  • First run for public office
  • Government relations and community outreach director
  • Environmental justice advocate in east Houston
  • Education: Milby High School; HCC Southeast; B.A. in finance and economics, University of St. Thomas; began graduate environmental studies at Rice University
